answer: we're at the'three results' bit. First, time of flight. Set y equal to zero again, solve for T, and you get T equals 2 v0 sine theta over g. Same as shown. Range ends up v0 squared sine 2 theta over g. And then maximum height comes from setting y dot to zero. So the peak is at t star equals v0 sine theta over g, which is half of T. Hmm, checking...Yeah.
